newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Albright to visit despite Cambodia fighting.
newsitem.headline: Albright to visit despite Cambodia fighting.

text.p: Heavy gun and mortar fire echoed through the Cambodian capital on Tuesday night, killing three party bodyguards as political tension between the country's two prime ministers boiled over.

The fighting, between irregulars of co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP) failed to dissuade U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright from visiting Phnom Penh next week.
Two bodyguards from FUNCINPEC and one bodyguard from the CPP were killed, officials and witnesses said.
A spokesman for Ranariddh's cabinet told Reuters the prince had called for calm.
"The prince has asked for patience and (asked people) not to use violence," the spokesman said.

U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Quinn said a mortar round crashed into the front yard of his residence, shattering its windows, and an American correspondent for Agence France Presse news agency was shot in the arm and slightly wounded, officials said.
Another FUNCINPEC bodyguard and taxi driver who had been in the area were injured and were being treated in a Phnom Penh hospital.

"There is no change in the plans the secretary of state. She plans to visit Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City and Phnom Penh next week before she goes into Hong Kong for reversion," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said in Washington.

Shooting broke out at the house of national police chief Hok Lundy in the city centre at about 10:30 p.m. (1530 GMT) and involved automatic weapons, mortars, grenades and possible tank rounds, witnesses reported.
The shooting sent residents running for their homes as police set up roadblocks and trucks of bodyguards raced through the city streets, Reuters photographer Patrick de Noirmont said.
The U.S. Embassy advised all American citizens to stay in their homes until further notice.
Monitored radio transmissions by the two factions indicated that Hun Sen's side had ordered tanks and multiple rocket launchers into the area where the shooting occurred.
But toward midnight (1700 GMT) the shooting died down and the city fell silent.

Government officials and diplomats told Reuters the clashes pitted armed units of the two parties against each other after a standoff at the house of national police chief Hok Lundy, a member of Hun Sen's party.

In a telephone interview with Reuters, Hok Lundy said bodyguards of Ranariddh armed with B40 rocket launchers had returned to his house for the second night in a row on Tuesday to intimidate his bodyguards.
"My bodyguards were suspicious and fired into the air and then they started shooting," he said.
Diplomats said the battle was a reflection of the political climate, which is only expected to worsen ahead of elections next year.
"Everyone is very itchy, and friction has obviously resulted," said one diplomat.

Ranariddh and Hun Sen, who were forced into a coalition government following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993, will oppose each other in polls. They have been feuding over a wide range of issues for over a year.
They have been heading for confrontation for some time but their disputes apparently came to a head over the government's response to Khmer Rouge strongman Pol Pot.

Pol Pot's Maoist rebels have been split over whether to make peace in their long war with the government. Pol Pot, mastermind of the genocidal 1975-79 "killing fields" regime, is said to be on the run in northern Cambodia.

Ranariddh wants to hasten their demise and forge political alliances with some of the rebels, while Hun Sen, who was with the Vietnamese invasion force that overthrew the rebels in 1979, has declared all talks with rebels illegal.
But both men want Pol Pot put before an international tribunal, a U.N. official said on Tuesday after meeting the two leaders.
